title: A Gujarat port just broke its own fastest-ever record - by breaking it even faster. November 12, 2026.
excerpt: From the founder of a university still running over a century later, to a Gujarat port that keeps beating its own records within weeks of setting them, November 12's two stories are about institutions and infrastructure built to outpace their own best previous version.
bodyHtml:
Today's two stories span 80 years, but share the same shape: something built once, that then kept getting better than its own prior best.

He founded a university that still runs today. Decades later, India gave him its highest civilian honor - after he was gone

Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, who died on November 12, 1946, founded Banaras Hindu University under the BHU Act of 1915 and served as its vice-chancellor until 1938. In 2014, 68 years after his death, India posthumously awarded him the Bharat Ratna, its highest civilian honor.

A Gujarat port just broke its own fastest-ever record - by breaking it even faster

Deendayal Port in Kandla, Gujarat, crossed 100 million tonnes of cargo for the financial year on October 6, 2026 - 51 days faster than it reached the same milestone the year before, which was itself the fastest ever at the time. Weeks earlier, the same port set a new all-India single-day cargo record, surpassing its own previous record set less than a month before.

Two stories, one pattern: an institution still educating generations a century after its founder, and a port that treats every one of its own records as something to beat again.
